q: Which of the following organelles is known as the "Translation Machinery" of the cell?
solution: Ribosomes are the cellular structures responsible for protein synthesis. They read the messenger RNA (mRNA) sequence and translate it into a string of amino acids, acting as the "translation machinery."

q: The "Nipun Bihar" scheme is primarily associated with which of the following sectors?
options: Foundational literacy and numeracy for school children
solution: The "Nipun Bihar" scheme was launched under the NIPUN Bharat Mission to ensure that every child in the state attains foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of Grade 3. Positive Marks: 1 Negative Marks: 0.25

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the "Appointment of an Acting Chief Justice" of the Supreme Court?
solution: Article 126 states that when the office of the Chief Justice of India is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform their duties, the President may appoint another Judge of the Court to perform the duties of the office.

q: In computer systems, the "Direct Memory Access" (DMA) is used to:
options: Increase the speed of the CPU
Allow I/O devices to transfer data directly to memory without constant CPU involvement
Connect the monitor to the motherboard
Store data permanently in the BIOS
solution: DMA is a feature of computer systems that allows certain hardware subsystems (like disk drives or sound cards) to access the main system memory independently of the central processing unit (CPU), thereby freeing up the CPU for other tasks.

q: The "Dalmia Nagar" industrial area in Bihar was historically famous for which industry?
solution: Dalmia Nagar (in Rohtas district) was one of the oldest and largest industrial towns in India, established by the Dalmia Group. It was famous for its massive production of sugar, cement, paper, and chemicals before its decline in the 1970s.

q: Which law in chemistry states that "at constant temperature and pressure, equal volumes of all gases contain an equal number of molecules"?
solution: Avogadro's Law states that under the same conditions of temperature and pressure, equal volumes of different gases contain an equal number of molecules (V ∝ n).

q: The "Lorenz Curve" cannot be used to measure which of the following?
solution: The Lorenz curve is a graphical representation used to represent the inequality of a distribution. It is standardly used for Income, Wealth, and Land holdings (assets). While theoretically applicable to any distribution, in standard economic contexts, "Population Density" is not a resource distribution measured by Lorenz curves in the same manner.

q: Which Indian state has launched the "Mukhya Mantri Sikho-Kamao Yojana" (Learn and Earn scheme)?
solution: The "Mukhya Mantri Sikho-Kamao Yojana" was launched by the Madhya Pradesh government to provide skills training and a stipend to unemployed youth.

q: The "Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary" is located in which physiographic division of Bihar?
solution: The Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Kaimur district, which falls under the Kaimur Range. This range is an eastern extension of the Vindhyan Range (Southern Hilly Region).

q: In MS-Excel, what is the keyboard shortcut to "Insert a New Worksheet"?
solution: Both Shift + F11 and Alt + Shift + F1 are valid keyboard shortcuts to insert a new worksheet in MS Excel. Ctrl + N creates a new workbook.

q: "Presbyopia" is a vision defect generally caused by:
options: Gradual weakening of ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the lens
solution: Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses its flexibility and the ciliary muscles weaken, making it difficult to focus on close objects.

q: During the 1857 Revolt, who was the Commissioner of Patna?
solution: William Taylor was the Commissioner of Patna during the Revolt of 1857. He is known for his harsh suppression of the uprising in the region.

q: Which of the following is a "Physical Change"?
solution: Sublimation of Iodine is a physical change because it involves a change of state (solid to gas) without altering the chemical composition of the iodine. The other options involve chemical reactions.

q: The "National Development Council" (NDC) was presided over by:
solution: The National Development Council (NDC) is an executive body presided over by the Prime Minister of India. It includes Union Ministers, Chief Ministers of all states, and NITI Aayog members.

q: "Barauni Refined Oil Pipeline" connects Barauni to which of the following cities?
solution: Barauni is a major pipeline hub. The Haldia-Barauni pipeline brings crude/products, and the Barauni-Kanpur pipeline transports refined products. Hence, it connects to both.

q: What is the keyboard shortcut to "Rename" a selected file or folder in Windows?
solution: Pressing F2 allows you to rename the currently selected file or folder in Windows Explorer.

q: Which vitamin is also known as "Antisterility Vitamin"?
solution: Vitamin E (Tocopherol) is known as the Anti-sterility Vitamin because its deficiency can lead to reproductive failure and sterility in some animals.

q: The "Eight Degree Channel" (8° N) separates which of the following?
solution: The Eight Degree Channel separates the islands of Minicoy (part of Lakshadweep, India) from the Maldives archipelago.

q: Which Fundamental Right cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency?
solution: According to the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978), the enforcement of the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 (Protection in respect of conviction for offenses) and 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

q: "Ransomware" attackers typically demand payment in which form?
solution: Attackers prefer cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin because they offer a high degree of anonymity and are difficult to trace compared to traditional banking methods.

q: The "Indrapuri Barrage" is built on which river?
solution: The Indrapuri Barrage is located across the Son River in the Rohtas district of Bihar. It is one of the longest barrages in India.

q: In economics, "The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money" was written by:
solution: Published in 1936, this book by John Maynard Keynes is considered the foundation of modern macroeconomics, introducing concepts like aggregate demand and the multiplier effect.

q: Which gas is used as a "Fruit Ripening Agent"?
"Duncan Passage" is situated between:
solution: The Duncan Passage is a strait in the Bay of Bengal that separates South Andaman Island from Little Andaman Island.

q: Which of the following is a "Network Layer" protocol?
solution: IP (Internet Protocol) operates at the Network Layer (Layer 3) of the OSI model, responsible for routing and addressing. TCP is Transport Layer, and HTTP/FTP are Application Layer.

q: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Patna High Court?
options: Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Chamier
solution: The Patna High Court was established in 1916. Its first Chief Justice was Sir Edward Maynard Des Champs Chamier.

q: The "New Collective Quantified Goal" (NCQG), recently discussed in COP29, is related to:
solution: The NCQG is a new global climate finance goal intended to replace the previous target of $100 billion per year, to be agreed upon by developed and developing nations to fund climate action.

q: "Sleeping Sickness" is caused by which of the following organisms?
solution: African Sleeping Sickness (African trypanosomiasis) is caused by the microscopic parasite of the species Trypanosoma brucei , transmitted by the tsetse fly.

q: The "Finance Commission" (Article 280) consists of a Chairman and how many other members?
solution: Article 280 provides that the Finance Commission shall consist of a Chairman and four other members to be appointed by the President.

q: "Cinnabar" is an ore of which metal?
solution: Cinnabar (Mercury(II) sulfide, HgS) is the bright scarlet to brick-red ore form of mercury and the most common source for refining elemental mercury.

q: The "Second Buddhist Council" was held during the reign of which king?
solution: The Second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali roughly 100 years after the Buddha's death, during the reign of King Kalasoka (Shishunaga dynasty).

q: In MS-Excel, which function returns the current system date and time?
solution: The NOW() function returns the current date and time. The TODAY() function returns only the current date.

q: "Operation Greens" was initially launched to stabilize the supply of "TOP" crops. What does "TOP" stand for?
solution: Operation Greens was announced in the 2018-19 budget to stabilize the supply and prices of Tomato, Onion, and Potato (TOP) crops, similar to Operation Flood for milk.

q: Which part of the human brain is the center for "Hunger and Thirst"?
solution: The Hypothalamus plays a crucial role in maintaining homeostasis, including the regulation of hunger, thirst, body temperature, and sleep.

q: The "91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003" limited the size of the Council of Ministers to what percentage of the total strength of the House?
solution: The 91st Amendment restricted the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers to not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (or State Assembly).

q: Which acid is present in "Vinegar"?
solution: Vinegar is essentially a dilute solution of Acetic Acid (CH3​COOH) in water (usually 5-8%).

q: Who founded the "Vikramshila University" in Bihar?
solution: Vikramshila University was established by the Pala Emperor Dharmapala (late 8th or early 9th century) in response to the decline in the quality of scholarship at Nalanda.

q: "Spam" is another name for:
solution: Spam refers to unsolicited commercial email (UCE) or unsolicited bulk email (UBE), typically sent to a large number of users for advertising or phishing.

q: Which district of Bihar has the highest density of population as per Census 2011?
solution: According to the 2011 Census, Sheohar has the highest population density in Bihar (1880 persons per sq. km), closely followed by Patna (1823 persons per sq. km).

q: "Tobin Tax" is a tax proposed on:
solution: Proposed by economist James Tobin, the Tobin Tax is a levy on spot currency conversions (international currency transactions) intended to discourage short-term currency speculation.

q: The SI unit of "Solid Angle" is:
solution: The Steradian (sr) is the SI unit of solid angle. Radian is the unit for plane angle.

q: In which year did the "Congress Socialist Party" hold its first session in Patna?
solution: The first formal conference of the Congress Socialist Party (CSP) was held in Patna in 1934, presided over by Acharya Narendra Deva, with Jayaprakash Narayan as General Secretary.

q: Which sorting algorithm is considered the "best" in the average case with a time complexity of O(n log n)?
solution: Quick Sort is generally considered the fastest sorting algorithm in the average case (O(nlogn)). Although its worst case is O(n2), it is usually faster than Merge Sort or Heap Sort in practice due to smaller constant factors and cache efficiency.

q: The "Ramsar Convention" is an international treaty for the conservation and sustainable use of:
solution: The Ramsar Convention (signed in Ramsar, Iran, in 1971) provides the framework for national action and international cooperation for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

q: Which tributary of the Ganga is also known as the "Kaligandaki" in Nepal?
solution: The Gandak River (also known as Narayani in Nepal) is formed by the union of the Kali Gandaki and Trisuli rivers.

q: The "Powerhouse of the Cell" is Mitochondria. Who discovered it?
solution: Richard Altmann discovered mitochondria in 1890 and called them "Bioblasts". The term "Mitochondria" was later coined by Carl Benda in 1898.

q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with "Equal Justice and Free Legal Aid"?
solution: Article 39A (Directive Principles of State Policy) obligates the State to promote justice and provide free legal aid to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.

q: In computer security, "AES" stands for:
solution: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is a symmetric block cipher chosen by the U.S. government to protect classified information and is used globally in software and hardware.

q: "Anugrah Narayan Sinha" was the first Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister of Bihar. He was popularly known as:
solution: Anugrah Narayan Sinha was affectionately called "Bihar Vibhuti". Dr. Rajendra Prasad was "Desh Ratna", and Jayaprakash Narayan was "Lok Nayak".

q: "Near Money" refers to assets that:
options: Are already in the form of cash
Can be easily converted into cash (like T-bills)
solution: Near money (or quasi-money) refers to highly liquid assets that can easily be converted into cash, such as savings accounts, government bonds, and treasury bills, but are not valid for immediate payments like currency.

q: What is the value of the "Gravitational Constant" (G)?
solution: The universal gravitational constant G is approximately 6.674×10−11Nm2/kg2. Option (b) is acceleration due to gravity (g).

q: Which Article provides for the "Establishment and Constitution of High Courts" for States?
solution: Article 214 states that there shall be a High Court for each State. Article 124 deals with the Supreme Court.

q: "Project Elephant" was launched in India in which year?
solution: Project Elephant was launched by the Government of India in 1992 to provide financial and technical support to major elephant-bearing states for the protection of elephants and their habitats.

q: In MS-PowerPoint, the shortcut to "Insert a Hyperlink" is:
solution: Ctrl + K opens the "Insert Hyperlink" dialog box. Ctrl + M inserts a new slide.

q: The "Great Indian Desert" is also known as:
solution: The Great Indian Desert is known as the Thar Desert, located primarily in the state of Rajasthan and extending into Pakistan.

q: "Heavy Water" (D2​O) is used in nuclear reactors primarily as a:
solution: Heavy water is primarily used as a moderator to slow down neutrons. Its low neutron absorption cross-section allows reactors (like PHWR) to use natural uranium as fuel. It often doubles as a coolant.

q: The "Tripuri Session" (1939) of the Congress is famous because:
options: Subhas Chandra Bose resigned as President
The Quit India resolution was passed
The National Planning Committee was set up
solution: At the Tripuri session, Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected as President against Gandhi's candidate (Pattabhi Sitaramayya). However, due to ideological differences with the Working Committee and Gandhi, Bose resigned shortly after.

q: What is the full form of "PNG" in computer graphics?
solution: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics. It is a raster-graphics file format that supports lossless data compression.

q: The "Kosi Project" is a joint venture between India and:
solution: The Kosi Project (involving the Kosi Barrage and embankments) is a result of a bilateral agreement between the Government of India and the Government of Nepal (signed in 1954).

q: Which hormone is secreted by the "Pineal Gland" to regulate the sleep-wake cycle?
solution: The Pineal Gland secretes Melatonin, often called the "sleep hormone," which regulates the circadian rhythm (sleep-wake cycle) in response to darkness.

q: "Disguised Unemployment" is a common feature in which sector of the Indian economy?
solution: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed in a job than are actually needed. This is most prevalent in the agricultural sector in India, where entire families work on small plots of land.

q: In the "Client-Server" model, which port is standard for "DNS" (Domain Name System)?
solution: Port 53 is the standard port used for DNS (Domain Name System) queries and responses. Port 80 is for HTTP, and 21 is for FTP.

q: The "Battle of Buxar" (1764) led to the signing of the:
solution: The Battle of Buxar ended with the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), signed between Robert Clive and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II (and the Nawab of Oudh), granting the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the East India Company.

q: What is the SI unit of "Magnetic Inductance" (Self or Mutual)?
solution: The SI unit of Inductance is the Henry (H). Tesla is for Magnetic Field strength, and Weber is for Magnetic Flux.

q: Which era is the official "National Calendar" of India based on?
solution: The National Calendar of India is based on the Saka Era (starting 78 AD). It was adopted on 22 March 1957.
